2. Problem Statement: 
Cancer is ranked among the significant causal factors of death globally and its management is marked by the complex way it interact with the immune system. Studies conducted in the present years have provided evidence that immune system has a significant influence on the cancer development and advancement. Thus, the elucidation of the precise nature and details of the tumor-immune system interface at the level of individual cells poses a major problem. This would help in development of better specific treatments for cancer, enhance the aspect of immunotherapy and, better identification of biomarkers in disease prognosis and progression.
One of the main problems in understanding tumor-immune relationships is the difficulty with the amount of data coming from RNA-seq method, which allows for the analysis of gene expression at low levels, namely, cells. Single-cell RNA-seq helps them to trace the heterogeneity within the tumor cells as well as the immune cells present in the vicinity. Nevertheless, this type of data is sometimes voluminous and can contain several variables that cannot be analyzed qualitatively. Tumor and immune cells are tightly connected tightly and their movements are more vigorous and also the spatial correlation between them also has profound influence on tumor progression, metastasis, and treatment outcome.
Most of the current approaches to diagnose tumor-immune interactions provide limited or more often rather simplistic views of these interactions. Prior work offers no method to analyze or considers shapes and changes which are apparent only with single-cell RNA-seq, or indeed does not consider immune cells or adjusts for tumor heterogeneity even if used on bulk tissue data. However, most of them do not fully make use of the graph-based representations of cellular interactions which can better describe the interactions between cells. Thus, there is a requirement to train/propose higher level computational models that can incorporate multi-faceted as well as high dimensional information derived from single cell RNA-seq, alongside with other dynamic crosstalk patterns between tumor and immune cells.
The challenge is that there is a persistent scarcity of the computational tools for modeling T-cells and tumor interactions at the single-cell level, while taking into consideration all the real-life aspects of cancer biology. Graph neural networks (GNNs) can indeed solve this problem effectively since they have been created with an ability to analyze and represent data based on graphs where the nodes are the cells and the edges are the interactions between the cells. Through a graph neural network, the current and functional topographical relationship between tumor cells and immune cells may be captured more truthfully, thereby permitting precise definition of their effects on cancer progression and responses to treatment.
All in all, the absence of comprehensive models of tumor immunity at the single-cell level remain an outstanding issue, which prevents optimization of cancer management. That is why this invention is designed to create a new graph neural network model to better represent and analyze the single-cell RNA-seq of tumor-immune interactions in order to advance the understanding of cancer and related therapies.


3.  Existing Solutions 
Most of the current methods to analyse the tumor-immune interactions involve bulk RNA sequencing where expression of thousands of genes is quantified from a combined sample of tumor and immune cells. Although these methods have advanced our knowledge in cancer, they offer a sample mean of activity of genes from billions of cells at once obfuscating heterogeneity of the sources of cancerous tissue. This is not ideal in terms of showing the differences between the cells or the interaction between tumor and immune system, which lowers the efficiency of cancer research and treatment.

To overcome this limitation, the most recent technique since a few years now used is the single-cell RNA sequencing commonly referred to as RNA-seq. It also permits quantification of gene expression on the single cell level that ID the different cells within the tumor mass and immune infiltration. This kind of detailed data may reveal how tumour cells interact with immune cells that were heretofore unknown possibly paves the way for development of better biomarkers and targets. However, they are inherently complex and multidimensional because single-cell RNA-seq is, and hence it is difficult to analyze with generic computational methods.

With the increase in the generation of single-cell RNA-seq data, various computational strategies have been introduced to work on the method, and they include clustering algorithms, dimensionality reduction techniques and machine learning. Several algorithms, which are k-means and hierarchical clustering can be used to cluster cells according to their gene expression, but these algorithms are unable to capture the cell dependencies as well as capability to model the spatial and functional conjunction between tumor and immune cells. t-SNE and UMAP are other techniques that are used to transform the high-dimensional gene expression profiles into lower dimensional spaces in the process of reducing their dimensions. The above mentioned methods are useful for presenting the data but there is no way to show how these cells interact and which of these interactions are responsible for tumor progression.

Some tumor-immune interaction models employ the ML algorithms, namely supervised ones such as random forest and SVM and unsupervised ones like an autoencoder. The earlier models created for cancer are used in prognosis or for treatment and are not accurate at individual cell and tumor immune interaction level. Further, these methods work under the assumption that tumor and immune environment are distinct and do not change over time as well as due to variations in the therapy.

Despite the advancements in learning with single-cell RNA-seq data and machine learning, there is no solution completely capitalized on graph nature of the tumor-immune system. Tumor cells and immune cells are extensively organized in space and their associations can be captured through a graph, where the nodes are the cells and the edges are the connections between the cells. Specifically, interactions are among the most challenging aspects in biological processes and are well suited for description in GNNs that have recently emerged in different fields. Nevertheless, the question of how a GNN can be employed to model T-IC interactions utilizing single-cell RNA-seq still has not been extensively investigated.

In conclusion, even though there has been much development in the study of the tumor-immune system through scRNA-seq, the current techniques fail to capture the intricacy of the system. Current techniques as a whole are not able to capture the dynamic behavior of the tumor-immune cell interactions and its underlying graph structure and cannot provide sufficient resolution to dissect further into the cancer biology and response towards the treatment. It becomes evident that there is a lack of GN that could incorporate cellular-level interactions between tumor cells and immune cells by using single-cell RNA-seq data in order to improve the modeling of cancer and consequently, enhance treatment.

6. Methodology 
The steps involved in the TI-GeM-GNNs for Single-Cell RNA-seq data are enstalled in the following steps that are intended to process and analyze high-resolution gene expression data for improving the understanding of tumor-Immune interactions at the single cell level. This methodology will help in modeling the interaction of these cells with the aid of GNNs to allow a dynamic and adaptive representation of the tumor immunity.
Step 1: Data Collection
The first one involves the collection of the single cell RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) from tumor samples. This data will offer the description of particular genes that are expressed in individual cells of the tumor and within the immune microenvironment. The important steps, which will be followed while collecting data includes:
• Tumor Cell Data: Molecular identification of proteins and nucleic acquiesces that are present in tumor cells. This sub-genre deals with gene expression data from immune cells the tumor micro-environment such as T cells, macrophages and dendritic cells.
• Spatial: Information about position and arrangement of the cells within the tumor tissue. This information is usually determined employing high-through-put single cellular RNA-seq methodologies, which quantitatively analyze the global transcripts of cells and dissect the physiological and structural diversity of the tumor and immune cells.
Step 2: Data Preprocessing
Once the single-cell RNA-seq data is obtained, the next procedure is data initialisation which entails cleaning and formatting of the data to meet the required format for the analysis:
• Standardization: Original RNA-seq quantification data are normalized in order to avoid that some cells were sequenced more deeply than others.
• Screening: This means that low quality cells have been screened out, and only the high quality data on gene expressions is to be used. 
• Selection of features where appropriate genes and markers are chosen for modeling based on the gene expression and the immunology and cancer progression processes.
• Data Conversion: The data is converted to suit a GNN format where each cells are represented as nodes while the interactions between cells as edges.
Step 3: Graph Construction
At this step, a graph is created in order to illustrate the connections between tumours and immune alterations. To prepare the graph, the following format is followed:
• Nodes: The nodes in the star graph correspond to the individual cells that can be either tumor or immune cells.
• Interactions between cells: Edges: This is the relationship between hormones, which is arrived at from the gene expression pattern and closeness between cells in the tissue. These may include intracellular signaling, mobility and contact between cells e.g via cytokines or adhesion molecules or antigen presentation. The nodes are of course the cells, and each node is defined with a feature vector, which is the gene expression profile of the cell.
• Special Features of Edges: The edges may also have special features that describe the likelihood of interaction between the cells or the kind of interaction they exhibit. This representation is temporal, and the GNN is able to learn intricate patterns of interaction between different cells in the tumor immune microenvironment.
• Bi: GNN Training – The fourth training is the Graph Neural Network (GNN) training, in which the accuracy of the knowledge graph is optimized by minimizing the empirical risk function concerning the loss function of the ground actual truth. 
Step 4: Train the GNN on the graph constructed towards modeling the tumor-immune interactions.
• Input: They include the information of source and target nodes (gene expression data) and are used as the initial input and information of the edges (interaction strength/type) into the graph convolutional neural network.
• GNN Architecture: GNN comprises of layers that increase the information from nearby nodes (cells) and learn patterns of interaction. The layers of the network are provided with message passing and data aggregation to transport the information from one cell to another, which enables the learning of spatial and functional aspects of tumor immune interactions by the network. However, when it came to prediction of adverse outcomes such as progression of tumor growth, immune evasion, and response to therapy, the loss function was created to enhance the model’s performance. It can include supervised learning with labelled data (e.g., tumor progression data) as well as the unsupervised learning to determine new relations.
• During the supervised training, the GNN tunes its parameters to predict the behaviors of tumor and immune cells after receiving their interaction fingerprints and also find out which biomarkers or interactions are significant for cancer progression and immune response.

Step 5: Tumor-Immune Interaction Analysis
Subsequently, the developed GNN is applied to the analysis of the tumor-immune interactions:
• Which and how ‘immunological interactions’ and immune cells is bundled by the GNN to preserve or advance tumor progression: The GNN can also predict how precisely tumor cells impact the activity of immune cells and which immune cells are participating in tumor progression, including ‘immune evasion mechanisms’.
• Immune features: The system finds out potential immune cells which are significant in tumor immune response that includes T cells activation, macrophage phenotypes, and antigen presentation.
• Treatment prediction: The GNN may be used for the prediction of the behavior of the tumors in response to immunotherapies, the options of which include checkpoint inhibitors or CAR-T cell therapies. This analysis is valuable for developing precise medicine approaches for treating the cancer, as it reveals the identities of the specific immune cells that contribute to the cancer growth and how they could be influenced with the oncological treatments.

Step 6: Continuous Model Updating
The last process is the complexity of the model improvement and its adaptation :
• Interactivity: The model is refined over time in the form of incorporating new samples of the tumor or new markers of the immune cell. This enables the GNN to learn new strategies of immune evasion by the tumor which may emerge in future.
• Feedback Loop: Therefore, if follow-up findings come out as part of the data that is being collected through ongoing research or clinical studies, the model can be easily adjusted to offer higher rates of precision and reliability.
This continuous adaptation also means that the system can remain relevant and effective in the assessment of the tumor-immune interactions for different cancer types and various therapeutic interventions.

Due to technological advancements, various industries face the most impact since blockchain technology offers unarguably the best way to record various transactions. Challenges that are experienced in analyzing blockchain transactions for fraud include; Current challenges of blocking numerous transactions as data is processed in real-time. The legacy fraud detection models are not fitted for real-time analysis and have static nature where alerts are generated by batch and/or rule-based algorithms. 3.  Existing Solutions 
Currently, there are many fraud detection systems present in blockchain for transactions, but they do not always provide the real-time solution required by the modern blockchain platforms especially when there are more transactions in the blockchain. The traditional methods of approach to detection of fraud in a blockchain context involve the use of rule-based approaches or static models that work batch wise on the transactional data. While the above techniques work well to detect traditional form of frauds like double-spend or an unauthorized access, do not fit in with the constantly evolving and relatively rapidly developing blockchain networks. They are also relatively slow in identifying new, hitherto unknown methods of fraud, hence the new and unforeseen loopholes in the system are always likely to be exploited.

Another existing solution is the application of machine learning, a type of artificial intelligence that is capable of analyzing large volumes of data with a view of identifying data patterns that could be an indication of fraud. However, these models are usually designed to work on vast data archives but are not fit for real-time data processing or their parameters cannot be easily updated as the new data is processed. It requires considerable time for the model’s training, and these models can hardly adapt in real-time to new fraud schemes or variations in the blockchain transactions. However, most of the current ML-based systems do not operate within sub-second latency, which is something that is needed to quickly detect and prevent blockchain transaction frauds that may happen at the rate of hundreds per second.

In addition, Bitcoin and Ethereum use PoW and PoS algorithms to provide confirmation of the carried out transactions and protect the network. Although these mechanisms assist in averting fraud by ensuring that through modifying the blockchain’s timeline it takes time for a fraudster to calculate, they do not immediately deter a fraudster from conducting unlawful activities. Consequently, the attackers can continuously use the system to affect their illegitimate activities until fraud detection mechanisms are deployed in identifying the problem.

Several blockchains have recently incorporated on-chain solutions and specific third-party fraud identification programs that look for any patterns of fraud within the transactions. However, these systems still remained batch based and however good they are in detecting anomalies do not provide the real time adaptive control component necessary to detect new and more complex fraudulent scenarios or even identify an initial stage of an attack.

As reported, the current methods used by these structures fail to meet the increasing demands of real-time fraud prevention on a blockchain. It is thus apparent that a real-time, AI-based fraud detection system that incorporates adaptive streaming analytics that can analyze the continuous flow of transaction chain and identify any emerging fraud patterns with sub-second response time to new types of fraud.

Description:TECHNICAL FIELD 
[0001] The present disclosure relates to fuel cell vehicles. More specifically, the present disclosure pertains to a system and a method for improving safety in a fuel cell vehicle.

BACKGROUND
[0002] Fuel Cell Vehicles (FCVs) are emerging as an environmentally friendly alternative to traditional internal combustion engine vehicles, offering a cleaner solution to transportation by utilizing hydrogen fuel cells to generate electricity. However, as hydrogen is a highly flammable gas, the safety of hydrogen storage and delivery systems is a primary concern in fuel cell vehicle design. 
[0003] Existing FCVs rely on hydrogen fuel cell units to power electric motors. These fuel cell units require a constant supply of hydrogen gas, typically stored in high-pressure tanks and delivered to the corresponding fuel cell unit through an inlet pipeline. The integrity of the inlet pipeline is critical for the safe operation of the vehicle, as any leakage of hydrogen gas from the pipeline can pose a serious safety risk due to hydrogen’s flammability and potential for explosive reactions. Traditionally, FCVs incorporate safety mechanisms to prevent hydrogen leakage, such as pressure relief valves, gas detection sensors, and emergency shutoff systems. However, such existing systems often detect leaks only after they have occurred, which means that damage to the vehicle and the risk to passengers and the environment may already be substantial. 
[0004] Existing FCVs often rely on gas sensors placed in various parts of the vehicle to detect hydrogen leaks. These sensors can measure hydrogen concentration in the air around the fuel cell system and activate safety mechanisms such as ventilation or emergency shut-off valves. However, these systems generally function in a reactive mode and can only respond once a leak has been detected, rather than preventing the leak itself. Modern FCVs may incorporate various sensors and systems to detect external impacts, such as accelerometers, collision detection algorithms, or damage assessment technologies. These systems can help detect when an accident occurs, but they typically cannot predict an accident or provide an early intervention mechanism to prevent damage to the hydrogen inlet pipeline or prevent leakage. 
[0005] Several safety mechanisms in conventional vehicles aim to reduce the risk of accidents, such as automatic braking systems, airbags, and stability control. These systems aim to prevent or mitigate accidents by actively controlling the vehicle’s behaviour based on sensor inputs. However, these safety mechanisms fail to focus particularly on preventing damage to the hydrogen infrastructure within an FCV or anticipate accident scenarios that could lead to dangerous hydrogen gas leaks. For example, patent document CN116742056A discloses a safety control system for a fuel cell vehicle that incorporates a combination of a temperature sensor, a pressure sensor, a hydrogen concentration sensor, and a collision sensor to assist in the proper functioning of the fuel cell vehicle. Another patent document, JP2004127748A, describes a fuel cell stack system equipped with a fuel cell control device that shuts off a hydrogen tank’s shutoff valve and reduces hydrogen in a downstream pipeline to an optimal level by allowing the corresponding fuel cell stack to continue power generation for a while when a gyroscope sensor detects that the acceleration of the hydrogen tank exceeds a prescribed value or a hydrogen sensor detects hydrogen leakage. However, such existing systems are reactive in nature, meaning they wait for an actual hazardous event, such as a collision or mechanical failure, to trigger safety measures. This reactive approach is insufficient in preventing accidents that may result from an undetected malfunction or in situations where an early warning could provide ample time to mitigate the hazard. 
[0006] Thus, while the existing technologies contribute to vehicle safety, they severely fail to fully address the risks associated with hydrogen-based FCVs. Specifically, they lack the ability to detect potential accidents or hazardous conditions in advance, particularly those that could compromise the hydrogen gas in the fuel supply infrastructure of an FCV. These existing systems are generally passive in detecting and responding to incidents, making them inadequate for preventing hydrogen leakage in the critical moments before or during an accident. Furthermore, existing safety measures are often implemented independently, without a comprehensive system that integrates accident prediction and pre-emptive safety intervention. This results in delayed responses and an increased risk of catastrophic failure. 
[0007] There is, therefore, a need for an improved solution that not only facilitates the prevention of hydrogen gas leakage in FCVs but also proactively detects such events before they occur. The present invention addresses the shortcomings or deficiencies associated with the prior art by enabling pre-emptive detection of events that may contribute to hydrogen gas leakage, offering enhanced safety mechanisms that ensure the hydrogen gas remains securely contained within the vehicle’s fuel supply infrastructure.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION
[0036] The following is a detailed description of embodiments of the disclosure depicted in the accompanying drawings. The embodiments are in such details as to clearly communicate the disclosure. However, the amount of detail offered is not intended to limit the anticipated variations of embodiments; on the contrary, the intention is to cover all modifications, equivalents, and alternatives falling within the scope of the present disclosures as defined by the appended claims.
[0037] Embodiments described herein relate to a system and method for enhancing safety in Fuel Cell Vehicles (FCVs) by preventing hydrogen gas leakage from a fuel supply infrastructure thereof. The system aims to proactively detect potential accidents or hazardous conditions before they occur, enabling early intervention to protect critical components of the vehicle’s hydrogen fuel supply infrastructure. By using various sensors and technologies, such as instability detection, collision detection, gas sensors, and accident prediction mechanisms, the system and method of the present disclosure ensure comprehensive safety for both vehicle occupants and the environment. The system can integrate seamlessly with existing vehicle control systems, improving response times and ensuring coordinated action to prevent accidents. 
[0038] FIG. 1 illustrates an exemplary schematic representation of a system 100 for improving safety in an FCV. The system 100 enables pre-emptive detection of potential accidents or hazardous conditions in the FCV, to trigger prevention of leakage of hydrogen gas from a fuel supply infrastructure of the FCV and ensure the safety of the vehicle occupants, surrounding individuals, and the environment.
[0039] The system 100 includes a fuel cell assembly (also referred to as “fuel cell stack” herein) 102 having an inlet pipeline 104 to receive supply of hydrogen gas from at least one hydrogen tank 106 of the FCV. The fuel cell stack 102 plays a central role in the operation of the FCV by facilitating an electrochemical reaction that generates electrical energy. The fuel cell stack 102 is made up of multiple fuel cells, each consisting of an anode, cathode, and an electrolyte membrane that enables the conversion of chemical energy into electrical energy. In operation, the hydrogen gas is supplied to an anode side of each fuel cell within the fuel cell stack 102. This hydrogen gas is typically stored in hydrogen tanks 106 capable of withstanding high pressure, and is delivered through the inlet pipeline 104. On an opposite side of the fuel cell stack 102, the cathode receives the oxygen gas, which is drawn from the ambient environment of the FCV, often through vents or air intakes in the vehicle. The fuel cell stack 102 combines the hydrogen gas with the oxygen gas in a controlled electrochemical process. During this reaction, the hydrogen molecules (H2) at the anode are split into protons (H?) and electrons (e?). The electrons travel through an external circuit, generating electric current that powers an electric motor of the FCV, which propels the FCV. Meanwhile, the protons pass through the electrolyte membrane of the fuel cell stack 102, which allows only positively charged ions to move between the anode and cathode, maintaining the electrochemical gradient necessary for the reaction. At the cathode, the protons, electrons, and oxygen molecules combine to form water (H2O), which is typically expelled as exhaust. The generated electricity is used to power the FCV’s electric motor, which drives the wheels of the FCV, providing a sustainable and emission-free alternative to conventional gasoline or diesel-powered vehicles. In addition to generating power, the fuel cell stack 102 may incorporate a thermal management system to regulate the temperature, ensuring the fuel cell stack 102 operates within optimal conditions. 
[0040] The system includes one or more sensors 108 configured to determine an event associated with leakage of the hydrogen gas from any of the inlet pipeline 104 or the hydrogen tank 102. The sensors 108 may be configured to determine the event associated with leakage of the hydrogen gas based on detection of a probability of accident of the FCV or any hazardous conditions that may compromise the hydrogen gas in the inlet pipeline 104 or the hydrogen tank 102. The sensors 108 may include one or more of gas sensors, accelerometers, gyroscopes, pressure sensors, temperature sensors, load cells, collision detection sensors, and vibration sensors, to monitor and assess the FCV’s safety and the integrity of the inlet pipeline 104 and/or the hydrogen tank 102.
[0041] The system 100 also includes a control unit 110 that is operatively coupled to the one or more sensors 108 and the fuel cell assembly 102. The control unit 110 plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety of the FCV by processing data received from the sensors 108 and making real-time decisions to mitigate potential hazards. Upon receiving data from the sensors 108, such as the detection of a potential accident or hazardous condition, indications of hydrogen leakage, abnormal pressure levels, and the like, the control unit 110 automatically activates proactive safety measures to ensure that the hydrogen gas remains securely contained within the hydrogen tank 106 and that any excess hydrogen gas present in the inlet pipeline 104 is efficiently drained or depressurized. Once the data received by the control unit 110 from the sensors 108 indicate that an event that could contribute to the leakage of hydrogen gas has occurred, the control unit 110 may take immediate corrective actions to prevent a fire or explosion hazard. These actions may include triggering emergency shutoff valves to stop the flow of hydrogen gas from the hydrogen tank 106 or the inlet pipeline 104, activating depressurization of the hydrogen gas present in the inlet pipeline 104 to safely release the excess hydrogen in a controlled manner, or even shutting down the fuel cell stack 102 to prevent further production of electrical power that might ignite the leaked hydrogen gas. 
[0042] In an exemplary embodiment, the control unit 110 may be configured to obtain a first instability data from an Advanced Driver-Assistance System (ADAS) of the FCV, obtain a second instability data from one or more load cells of the sensors 108 configured with the wheels of the FCV, and determine roll and yaw rate data from at least one accelerometer sensor installed in the FCV. The control unit 110 may compare each of the first instability data, the second instability data, and the roll and yaw rate data with corresponding threshold values to determine the probability of accident of the FCV, to assess whether such event can contribute to the leakage of hydrogen gas from the FCV’s fuel supply infrastructure.
[0043] The system 100 may include a notification unit 112 configured to notify one or more users of the FCV, upon determination of the event associated with leakage of the hydrogen gas by the one or more sensors 108. The control unit 110 may be operatively coupled to the notification unit 112 to send alerts to the FCV’s on-board diagnostic system or the driver to inform them of the detected leakage, allowing them to take appropriate action. Additionally, the control unit 110 may be configured to activate warning lights or alarms to notify the occupants of the risk. By integrating these various safety measures, the control unit 110 ensures that the FCV can respond quickly and effectively to prevent catastrophic failure, thus significantly reducing the risk of fire hazards or other consequences resulting from hydrogen leakage. The control unit 110 also continuously monitors the status of the FCV’s fuel supply infrastructure, ensuring that safety mechanisms are always active and ready to intervene if necessary.
[0044] When the sensors 108 detect the occurrence of an event associated with the leakage of hydrogen gas from the inlet pipeline 104, the control unit 110 is configured to take immediate and precise action to prevent further risk of hydrogen gas leakage or potential hazards. In an exemplary embodiment, the system 100 may include a plurality of shutoff valves positioned at the inlet pipeline 104. The control unit 110 may be configured to regulate actuation of the shutoff valves to isolate the hydrogen tank 106 from the fuel cell assembly 102. The control unit 110 isolates the hydrogen tank 106 from the fuel cell assembly 102 by activating appropriate shutoff valves or other mechanisms that block the flow of hydrogen gas through the inlet pipeline 104. This step ensures that no additional hydrogen gas is supplied from the hydrogen tank 106 to the fuel cell assembly 102, thus preventing further leakage and reducing the risk of a fire or explosion. Once the hydrogen tank 106 is successfully isolated from the fuel cell assembly 102, the control unit 110 then operates the fuel cell assembly 102 at a pre-determined capacity, to initiate a controlled depressurization process. The purpose of this depressurization is to safely burn or utilize any excess hydrogen gas that is still present in the inlet pipeline 104 to generate electricity, thereby reducing the pressure within the inlet pipeline 104 and minimizing the risk of additional leakage. In an exemplary embodiment, the electricity generated by processing the excess hydrogen gas may be delivered by the fuel cell assembly 102 to any or a combination of the electric motor, a brake resistor and a battery pack of the FCV. 
[0045] By carefully controlling the operation of the fuel cell assembly 102 at the pre-determined capacity, the control unit 110 ensures that the depressurization process is gradual and controlled, further preventing any sudden pressure changes or potential ruptures in the inlet pipeline 104. The control unit 110 isolates the hydrogen tank 106 and depressurizes the inlet pipeline 104 to stop the immediate risk of hydrogen leakage. The control unit 110 may be operatively connected to the sensors 108 to continuously monitor the pressure levels of the hydrogen gas within the inlet pipeline 104 and the status of the fuel cell assembly 102, ensuring that these corrective actions are implemented efficiently and effectively.
[0046] The control unit 110 may be configured to determine the pre-determined capacity for operating the fuel cell assembly 102 based on a first set of parameters, which include at least one of a maximum power limit of the brake resistor, a State-of-Charge (SoC) of the battery pack, a maximum charge limit of the battery pack, and a current recuperation power value of the battery pack. For example, the maximum power limit of the brake resistor can indicate how much energy is available to dissipate from the fuel cell stack 102. The State-of-Charge (SoC) of the battery pack reflects the current energy level of the battery pack, which helps the control unit 110 determine how much power is available for operation of the fuel cell stack 102. Similarly, the maximum charge limit of the battery pack provides the upper limit of energy that can be stored on the battery pack, while the current recuperation power value of the battery pack informs the control unit 110 about the energy that can be recuperated or recharged during braking or deceleration of the FCV. The first set of parameters may include other parameters that provide essential information about current operating conditions of the fuel cell stack 102, the brake resistor and the battery pack of the FCV. The control unit 110 may be configured to continuously monitor the first set of parameters and compare each with its corresponding threshold value. These threshold values are pre-configured limits based on the specific design and operating characteristics of the fuel cell stack 102. By comparing the actual values of each of the first set of parameters with their threshold values, the control unit 110 determines the optimal pre-determined capacity at which the fuel cell assembly 102 should be operated to ensure the hydrogen gas within the inlet pipeline 104 is safely and efficiently depressurized. The ability to dynamically adjust the operating capacity of the fuel cell assembly 102 based on real-time data allows the control unit 110 to ensure that the depressurization process does not interfere with the vehicle’s overall energy requirements and safety protocols. Thus, the control unit 110 can achieve a balance between maintaining vehicle performance and effectively reducing pressure of the excess hydrogen gas in the inlet pipeline 104, thereby preventing any risks associated with hydrogen leakage.
[0047] The control unit 110 may be configured to validate the completion of the depressurization of excess hydrogen gas in the inlet pipeline 104 based on a second set of parameters that reflect the status of both the excess hydrogen gas and the operation of the fuel cell assembly 102. The second set of parameters may include, among other factors, the energy of the excess hydrogen gas present within the inlet pipeline 104, the pre-determined capacity of the fuel cell assembly 102 determined based on the first set of parameters, and the actual power output of the fuel cell assembly 102 at the instance when the event associated with hydrogen leakage is detected by the sensors 108. 
[0048] To ensure the depressurization process has been properly executed, the control unit 110 may be configured to accurately assess the energy of the hydrogen gas that was present in the inlet pipeline 104 at the time of detection of the event associated with the leakage of the hydrogen gas from the inlet pipeline 104. The energy of the hydrogen gas is typically calculated using a combination of key parameters, such as the volume, pressure, and temperature of the hydrogen gas. These factors, when measured accurately at the instance of the detected event, can provide the control unit 110 a precise determination of the energy level of the hydrogen gas. Once the energy of the hydrogen gas is determined, the control unit 110 uses this information to compare it with the pre-determined capacity of the fuel cell assembly 102. This comparison results in the calculation of a first threshold parameter, which represents the difference between the energy of the hydrogen gas in the inlet pipeline 104 and the pre-determined capacity. The control unit 110 also calculates a second threshold parameter, which compares the energy of the hydrogen gas in the inlet pipeline 104 with the actual power output of the fuel cell assembly 102 at the time the leakage event is detected. By continuously monitoring the power output of the fuel cell stack 102, the control unit 110 can assess whether the depressurization process is successfully decreasing the energy of the hydrogen gas within the inlet pipeline 104. Specifically, the control unit 110 compares the first and second threshold parameters. If the control unit 110 determines that the power output of the fuel cell stack is consistently decreasing over time, the control unit 110 ascertains that the excess hydrogen gas is being depressurized effectively. This allows the control unit 110 to evaluate that the depressurization process is complete and successful, ensuring that the excess hydrogen gas in the inlet pipeline 104 is safely managed, and that no further risk of leakage or hazardous situations remains. 
[0049] In an exemplary embodiment, the control unit 110 may be implemented using various hardware configurations or a combination of software and hardware features. For instance, the control unit 110 may incorporate microcontrol units, switches, relays, gates, and specialized hardware features like application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), electrically erasable programmable read-only memories (EEPROMs), or field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). In some cases, memory components like non-volatile random access memory (RAM) or read-only memory (ROM) may also form part of the control unit 110. In another embodiment, the control unit 110 may be entirely software-based, operating either as part of an operating system or as an application running on one. The control unit 110 may be connected to the fuel cell stack 102, the sensors 108, and the notification unit 112 either wirelessly or in a wired manner.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to an adaptable tooth brush holding and cleaning device that is able to hold a toothbrush securely according to its size, thus making sure it is tightly fastened for the following cleaning procedures.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002]  Maintaining oral hygiene is essential, and manual toothbrushes have long been the primary tool for brushing teeth. Typically, users hold the toothbrush manually and move it across their teeth to clean them. Various traditional holders have been used to keep toothbrushes in place or to simplify their use, such as simple stands or wall-mounted brackets. However, these holders often lack features for ensuring effective cleaning or may not be ergonomically designed, leading to less thorough brushing. They also do not address issues like ensuring the brush is used at the optimal angle or maintaining brush hygiene between uses.

[0003] Conventionally, toothbrush holders were often made from ceramic, metal, or glass and were designed to keep the toothbrush upright and dry. These simple designs included wall-mounted holders, countertop cups, and drawer trays. These holders provided basic functionality but did not address all needs. And people use to clean these brushes manually via water after usage. But the method is limited to precision. Hence, an equipment needs to be developed that holds and clean tooth brushes in an effective manner. 

[0004] US5480038A discloses about an invention that includes a reversibly mounted holder for storing toothbrushes within a gap defined between a platform and an adjacent plate, the toothbrush being further attached to the holder by a coiled strap to prevent removal of the toothbrush from the immediate vicinity. Although US’038 relates to a toothbrush holder. But the cited invention lacks in detecting and removing food residues from the toothbrush bristles. 

[0005] US9226571B1 discloses about an invention that includes a device for cleaning a toothbrush, attachable to a faucet expelling water in a first direction, the device including: an adapter mountable on a water expelling end of the faucet; and a cylindrical cleaning element in fluid flow communication with the adapter and disposed, when the adapter is mounted on the faucet, in a direction transverse to the first direction, the cylindrical cleaning element including a cylindrical housing and a water expelling cylindrical element, disposed within the cylindrical housing and including multiple rows of circumferentially disposed nozzles for expelling water jets, the water expelling cylindrical element defining an interior space accessible via circular portal at an end thereof, wherein when water is expelled from the faucet, at least some water is directed in the transverse direction and expelled through the nozzles in the water expelling cylindrical element. Though US’571 relates to a device for cleaning a toothbrush. But the cited invention fails to cover the toothbrush head with a protective enclosure that prevents contamination when the toothbrush is not in use. 
 
[0006] Conventionally, many devices have been developed that are capable of holding and cleaning toothbrushes. However, these devices are incapable of detecting and removing food residues from the toothbrush bristles. Additionally, these existing devices also fails to cover the toothbrush head with a protective enclosure that prevents contamination when the toothbrush is not in use.

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that requires to be capable of detecting and removing food residues from the toothbrush bristles, thereby ensuring the bristles are clean and ready for use. In addition, the developed device also needs to cover the toothbrush head with a protective enclosure that prevents contamination when the toothbrush is not in use, thus maintains hygiene.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]  The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]  An object of the present invention is to develop a device that secures a toothbrush in place based on its dimensions, thereby ensuring it is firmly held for subsequent cleaning processes.

[0010] Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of detecting and removing food residues from the toothbrush bristles, thereby ensuring the bristles are clean and ready for use.

[0011] Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that cover the toothbrush head with a protective enclosure that prevents contamination when the toothbrush is not in use, thus maintains hygiene.
     
[0012]  The foregoing and other objects, features, and advantages of the present invention will become readily apparent upon further review of the following detailed description of the preferred embodiment as illustrated in the accompanying drawings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0013]  The present invention relates to an adaptable tooth brush holding and cleaning device that is capable of identifying and eliminating food particles from the toothbrush bristles to ensure they are thoroughly cleaned and prepared for use.

[0014]  According to an embodiment of the present invention, an adaptable tooth brush holding and cleaning device, comprises of a cylindrical hollow body developed to be positioned on a fixed surface, plurality of suction units are arranged underneath the body to adhere to the surface for securing the body on the surface, a slot carved in the body for enabling a user to accommodate a toothbrush, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit installed on the body and to determine dimensions of the toothbrush handle, a motorized iris operated lid integrated on top portion of the body, to get closed for gripping the handle, in view of securing the toothbrush in the slot, a hollow cuboidal member arranged with the body by means of an extendable inverted  L-shaped rod that extend/retract for positioning the member on the toothbrush head, a motorized iris operated aperture integrated on the member for getting opened/closed to cover the member over the head, thus preventing contamination of bristles of the tooth brush, plurality of pneumatic pins arranged in the member by means of a two-axis slider, a dust sensor is embedded in the member for determining deposition of any food residues in the bristles of head, based on which the pins extend/retract to get deployed in between the bristles, to provide required two-axis translation to the pins, for moving the pins over the residues, in view of removing the residues, and a water storage chamber having a first section stored with clean water, and a second section designated to collect dirty water.

[0015] According to another embodiment of the present invention, the proposed device further comprises of an electronically controlled nozzle is configured with the chamber, for dispensing clean water over the brush head, via a conduit, in view of rinsing the brush head, thereby cleaning the brush head, while the waste water is collected in the second section during cleaning, a UV (Ultraviolet) lamp integrated in the member to project ultraviolet rays onto the bristles, in view of sterilizing the bristles,  thus facilitating the user in cleaning and disinfecting the bristles, a motorized circular slider is installed in between the rod and body for providing translation to the rod, as per the user’s position as detected by a proximity sensor embedded in the body, a laser measurement sensor is embedded in the member for determining gaps in between the bristles, a microphone integrated in the body for enabling the user to interact with the device through voice commands, regarding positioning/retrieval of the brush in/from the body, thereby facilitating hands-free operation and a battery is configured with the device for providing a continuous power supply to electronically powered components associated with the device.

The microcontroller processes the received signals in order to analyze the voice inputs of the user and upon analyzing the voice commands the microcontroller actuates the device and accordingly commands the device to carry out positioning of the brush in the body 101.

[0028]  Post positioning of the toothbrush within the body 101, on the slot 103 the microcontroller generates a command and actuates an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 104 which is installed on the body 101. [0029]  The imaging unit 104 disclosed herein comprises of an image capturing arrangement including a set of lenses that captures multiple images of the body 101 and the captured images are stored within memory of the imaging unit 104 in form of an optical data. [0033] Th rod 107 gets positioned in a user-specified position which is determined via a proximity sensor that is embedded in the body 101. The proximity sensor consists of an emitter and a receiver. [0034]  The member 106 is installed with a motorized iris operated aperture 108, which works in the same manner as of iris lid 105 and on actuation gets opened/closed to cover the member 106 over the head, thus preventing contamination of bristles of the tooth brush.

A photo sensor and an infrared light-emitting diode which is known as an infrared LED are optically arranged in the dust sensor. The photo-sensor detects the reflected infrared LED rays which are bounced off of the dust particles present over the bristles The reflected infrared LED rays are converted into an analog value which is further converted into an electrical signal, wherein the electrical signal is sent to the microcontroller. [0038] The laser measurement sensor emits a laser beam which is usually in the form of a focused, collimated light beam that hits the bristles surface, it gets reflected back towards the sensors. The sensor precisely measures the time it takes for the laser beam to travel to the bristles surface and return. Using the speed of light as a constant the sensor calculates the distance between itself and the bristles surface. The laser measurement sensor collects a significant amount of data by scanning the entire surface of the bristles and forms a 3D point cloud, which represents the shape of the bristles. The laser measurement sensor sends the data to a microcontroller which processes the acquired data and detects the gaps in between the bristles.

Thereby, on actuation it sterilizes the bristles, in view of facilitating the user in cleaning and disinfecting the bristles.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to an adjustable toddler accommodation assistive device for trolley bags capable of assisting a user to accommodate a toddler comfortably while traveling, and also capable of detecting the environmental conditions like rain/sunrays to protect the toddler from rain/sunrays.  

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Accommodating toddlers with baggage involves providing suitable arrangements and amenities that cater to the needs of young children and their families during travel or in various settings like hotels and public transportation. This includes ensuring that there are child-friendly spaces, such as play areas or cribs, and offering practical solutions like baby carriers, strollers, and storage for diapers, snacks, and other essentials. The goal is to make the experience comfortable and convenient for both the child and the parents, reducing stress and ensuring that all necessary items are easily accessible.

[0003] Traditional methods of accommodating toddlers with baggage often involve using bulky and cumbersome items like large diaper bags, strollers, and car seats, which can be challenging to manage, especially in crowded or confined spaces. These methods may lead to difficulties with maneuverability, such as navigating tight aisles in airplanes or cramped spaces in hotels. Additionally, traditional diaper bags and travel gear can quickly become disorganized, making it hard for parents to find essentials quickly. This results in increased stress and inconvenience, as parents struggle to juggle the needs of their child with the logistics of traveling or managing their environment.

The supporting rod is provided with a sliding seat capable of sliding along the supporting rod and the sliding seat is provided with a locking position capable of being locked or unlocked with the locking seat when the sliding seat slides along the supporting rod. The device is simple in structure and good in safety. Although CN’280 is related to toddler accommodation assistive device. A linkage piece capable of rotating relative to the front leg and the supporting rod assembly  is arranged between the front leg and the supporting rod assembly, one end of the linkage piece is rotationally connected to the front leg around a third axis, the other end of the linkage piece is rotationally connected to the supporting rod assembly around a fourth axis , and when the linkage piece rotates relative to the front leg  around the third axis , the front leg  and the rear leg  can rotate and get close to each other. The folding chair is simple in structure and small in size after being folded. Although CN’463 is related to a toddler accommodation assistive device. However, the cited art is incapable of monitoring the surrounding of the toddler for providing protection from rain and sunrays.
 
[0006] Conventionally, many devices related to toddler assistive device that are incapable of accommodating a toddler while traveling from one place to another while determining the dimensions of the toddler for comfortably accommodating the toddler. 

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device capable of accommodating the toddlers according to their dimensions for providing comfort to toddler.

[0022] Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of an adjustable toddler accommodation assistive device for trolley bags is illustrated, comprising a hollow cuboidal body 101 developed to be positioned on a trolley bag, a pair of C-shaped clamps 102 installed on lateral sides of the body 101, each by means of a telescopically operated rod 103, a motorized ball and socket joint 104 is integrated in between the rod 103 and clamp, a cushioned member 105 installed over the body 101, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 106 integrated in the body 101, a drawer arrangement 107 integrated in the body 101, a sensing module 108 is embedded in the body 101, a pair of inverted U-shaped frames 109 arranged on lateral sides of the body 101, a motorized slider lid 110 installed over the frame, actuates a speaker 111 installed on the body 101 and an inverted U-shaped shaft 112 installed on back portion of the body 101, electromagnetic springs 113 arranged in between said body 101.

[0023] The proposed device comprises a hollow cuboidal body 101 developed to be positioned on a trolley bag, which is preferably made of soft plastic due to safety issues of the toddler. An ultrasonic sensor is integrated on the body 101 for determining the position of the handle of the trolley bag. The ultrasonic sensor operates by emitting high-frequency sound waves from a transducer which travels to the handle of the trolley bag and reflects to the sensor. The sensor measures the time it takes for the sound waves to return after bouncing back from the handle. This time delay is used to calculate the position of the handle. Then an inbuilt microcontroller actuates a pair of C-shaped clamps 102 installed on the lateral sides of the body 101 connected via a telescopically operated rod.

[0024] The clamps 102 mentioned above are motorized clamps 102 actuated by the microcontroller to grip the handle of the trolley. The motorized clamps 102 works by using an electric motor connected to a sliding jaw via a screw. The motor provides power to the screw that is attached to the fixed frame of the clamp. As the screw rotates, it pushes or pulls the sliding jaw towards or away from the fixed jaw depending on the direction of rotation. This movement allows the clamp to grip the handle of the trolley. The telescopically operated rod 103 actuated to by the microcontroller pneumatically to position the C-shaped clamps 102 near the handle of the trolley.

[0025]  The pneumatic unit powers the telescopic rods, wherein the pneumatic unit embodies an air compressor, air cylinder, air valves, and piston which work in collaboration to perform the extension and retraction of the rods. The rod 103 comprises a nested tube arrangement that contains multiple hollow tubes connected concentrically. The air cylinder is attached to the bottom of the nested tube arrangement and further consists of an air piston attached to the topmost part of the nested tube arrangement from the inside. The air cylinder is integrated with one inlet and one outlet valve that is connected to an air compressor configured with an exhaust fan. The air compressor draws air from the surroundings and compresses it to form pressurized air which enters the inlet valve and creates a force that pushes the piston in the forward direction. As the piston moves in the forward direction, it leads to the sequential opening of the concentrically connected tubes from the top toward the bottom. This leads to the extension of the rod 103 towards the handle of the trolley. To retract the rod, the pressurized air is taken back into the compressor from the outlet valve which makes the piston move in a backward direction causing the retraction of the rod. The clamps 102 and rod 103 are connected via a motorized ball joint for providing an omnidirectional movement.

[0026] The motorized ball and socket joint 104 allows for smooth, adjustable movement in Omni directions and has a ball-shaped part that fits into a cup-like socket. A motor controls this ball, making it move around inside the socket. Actuators adjust the ball’s position to ensure it moves accurately and flexibly, enabling precise control and positioning in multiple directions.

[0027] A cushioned member 105 installed over the body 101 for allowing the user to accommodate the toddler on the member. An artificial intelligence based imaging unit 106 linked with a processor installed on the body 101 for capturing multiple images of the toddler and in vicinity of the body 101. Processor process the captured images for determining the dimensions of the toddler. The imaging unit comprises of a camera that captures a high-resolution image of toddler and in vicinity of the body 101. Then, the processor extracts the required feature from the image which includes first pre-processing of the image to enhance clarity and identify the dimensions of the toddler using the algorithms via artificial intelligence. The processor then sends the detected dimension to the microcontroller. Based on these dimensions the microcontroller actuates a drawer arrangement 107 integrated in the body 101 to increase/decrease the dimensions of the body 101 for providing a comfortable accommodation to the toddler in the body 101.

[0028] The drawer arrangement 107 comprises of two plates which are connected through a slider. The slider consists of a sliding rail and a motorized slid able member connected to the sliding rail. The motorized slid able member is attached in the body 101 and further to a motor which provides movement to the member in a bi-directional manner and proving the movement to the plates. This way the drawer arrangement 107 expands/contracts in accordance with the detected dimension accommodating the toddler in the body 101 comfortably.

[0029]  A sensing module 108 is integrated in the body 101 for detecting presence of rain and reflection of the sun rays over the toddler. A rain sensor is linked with the module to detect the rain over the toddler. The rain sensor detects rain by utilizing conductive plates arranged in a gird. When the raindrops fall on the sensor, they create a conductive path between the plates causing the change in electrical resistance. The change is detected by the sensor and converted into an electrical signal which is further translated to the microcontroller.

[0030] A sunlight detecting sensor is also integrated in the module to detect the sun light over the toddler, the sunlight sensor works by detecting the amount of light falling on it. It typically has a light-sensitive component, like a photodiode or a light-dependent resistor, which changes its electrical properties in response to the light it receives. When the sensor is exposed to sunlight, it produces a signal that can be measured and used to determine the intensity of the light. This signal helps devices adjust their functions accordingly, such as dimming or brightening screens, or turning lights on or off, to make the most efficient use of natural light. And bases of received signals the microcontroller actuates a pair of U shaped frames integrated with a motorized slider lid 110 arranged on the lateral sides of the body 101, to deploy the lid over the toddler to protect the toddler from the detected rain and sunrays.

[0031] The sliders installed between the frame and the body 101 consist of a sliding rail and a motorized slidable member connected to the sliding rail. The motorized slidable member is attached to the body 101 and frame on both sides to make the body 101 slide. The slidable member is attached to a motor which provides movement to the member in a bi-directional manner to protect the toddler form the rain and sunrays.

[0032]  A moisture sensor is integrated on the cushioned member 105 to detect presence of moisture on the body 101, wherein the moisture sensor designed to detect temperature operates by using a temperature-sensitive element, such as Resistance Temperature Detector (RTD), which changes its electrical resistance with temperature variations. As the temperature rises or falls, the resistance of the element changes accordingly. This change in resistance is converted into an electrical signal by the sensor's circuitry, which then send the electric signals to the microcontroller, further actuates a speaker 111 installed in the body 101 to provide audio notifications to the user regarding removal of the moisture from the body 101.

[0033] The speaker 111 works by converting the electrical signal into the audio signal. The speaker 111 consists of a cone known as a diaphragm attached to a coil-shaped wire placed between two magnets. When the electric signal is passed through the voice coil, then coil generates a varying magnetic field that interacts with the magnet causing the diaphragm to move back and forth. This movement pushes and pulls air creating sound waves just like the electrical signal received and used to notify the user.

[0034]  An inverted U-shaped shaft 112 is installed on back portion of the body 101 to be gripped by the user for moving the bag, along with the toddler, thereby facilitating the user in carrying the toddler. An impact sensor is installed in the body 101 for monitoring any shocks experienced by the body 101 due to movement of the trolley bag on the surface, the impact sensor used here consists of strain gauges that work on the principle that the electrical resistance of a conductor changes with deformation. The strain gauge is a thin metallic foil arranged in a grid pattern. When the platform experiences some shock, the gauge attached and the foil are deformed, causing a change in its electrical resistance. This change in resistance is converted into a voltage signal by the sensor providing the measurement of the strain. These signals further transmitted to the microcontroller, which further actuates plurality of electromagnetic springs 113 arranged in between the body 101 and member to expand/contract for absorbing the shocks to provide comfortable experience to the toddler.

[0035] When an electrical current flows through the coil of the electromagnet, coil generates a magnetic field. The strength of this field is proportional to the amount of current. When a sudden impact or force is experienced by the platform it affects the attached electromagnetic spring. The impact causes the spring to compress or extend in response. The electromagnetism is adjusted to vary the spring’s stiffness and handle different impact forces. Increasing the current strengthens the magnetic field, which can compress the spring more or extend it, depending on the setup.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention pertains to food decorating and more specifically to an edible food items decoration assistive device that helps users decorate edible items by dispensing a precisely regulated amount of decorative edibles according to the user’s specified design, ensuring both ease of use and accuracy in achieving the desired decorative effect.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002]  Food decoration enhances the visual appeal of dishes, making them more inviting and appetizing. Food decoration is essential in both culinary presentations and dining experiences, as it engages the senses and elevates the perceived quality of the meal. Artistic food decoration not only attracts attention but also stimulates the appetite, making meals more enjoyable and memorable. In professional settings like restaurants and catering, food decoration reflects the chef’s creativity and attention to detail, contributing to the overall dining experience. For home cooks, food decoration adds a touch of elegance and care, making everyday meals feel special. Additionally, food decoration is important in special events and celebrations, where visually stunning presentations enhance the occasion's festive atmosphere and contribute to the overall enjoyment.

[0003] Traditional food decoration methods include garnishing with fresh herbs, edible flowers, and intricate piping of sauces or creams. These techniques enhance visual appeal and add flavor, but these techniques come with drawbacks. Garnishing requires careful selection and preparation of ingredients, which can be time-consuming and may not always stay fresh for long. Edible flowers can be expensive and limited by seasonality. Piping intricate designs can be skill-intensive and prone to inconsistencies. Additionally, these methods often demand a high level of manual effort and artistry, which may not be feasible for every cook or occasion. Furthermore, traditional methods may not always align with modern dietary trends or accommodate dietary restrictions, potentially limiting their applicability.

[0004] WO2004041548A1 is a cake decorating device, suitable for producing a more dramatic and attractive atmosphere of the place where various celebratory events are held, while displaying a congratulation message or picture on the decorating device by heat conduction. The cake decorating device includes a base having locking grooves formed at an upper surface of the base, and a support plate having locking protrusions formed at a lower surface of the support plate to be fitted into the locking grooves of the base. The support plate has a plurality of candles. Also, a transfer paper having a message printed using a thermosensitive microcapsule product is attached onto a wall of the base, whereby the message can be displayed by heat conduction of the candles. Thus, the atmosphere of the celebratory event is beautifully produced and reaches the climax by the cake decorating device. Though WO’548 relates to cake decorating devices, and, more specifically, to a cake decorating device for use in producing a more dramatic and attractive atmosphere of the place, however this cited prior art lacks in assisting a user in icing onto a cake as per dimensions of the cake hindering professional-quality results, increasing physical efforts, and prohibiting for intricate designs and smooth, even coverage.

[0005] US10019842B2 relates to an augmented reality system for a food product includes an edible media or a food product decoration with an embedded augmented reality marker and a related application for a mobile device. The application presents augmented reality content associated with the augmented reality marker. The application permits access to the augmented reality content in response to detection of the application recognizing the embedded augmented reality marker. Although US’842 discloses an augmented reality system for a food product, however this cited prior art is inadequate of assisting a user in icing onto a cake as per dimensions of the cake, thereby impeding the achievement of professional-quality results, increasing physical effort, and preventing the creation of intricate designs and smooth, even coverage.

[0006] Conventionally, many devices have been develop that relates to food decorating devices, however these devices are generally inadequate for assisting users in icing cakes according to the specific dimensions, which significantly hampers the attainment of professional-quality results, necessitates increased physical effort, and obstructs the creation of intricate designs and smooth, even coverage, thus limiting their effectiveness and precision in achieving a high level of cake decoration that meets the desired standards.

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that aids the user in decorating food items by dispensing a precisely regulated amount of decorative edibles based on the user’s specified design, thereby ensuring both ease of use and accuracy in achieving the desired decorative effect, ultimately facilitating professional-quality results and reducing the effort required for intricate designs and smooth, even coverage.

[0022]  Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of an edible food items decoration assistive device is illustrated, comprising a circular housing 101 having plurality of compartments 102, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 103 mounted on the body, a holographic projection unit 104 mounted over the body, a motorized iris unit 105 crafted on each of the compartments 102, a hollow telescopic pole 106 installed in continuation to the iris unit 105, plurality of electromagnetic springs 107 configured inside the body, and a speaker 108 mounted on the body.

[0023] The device proposed herein includes a circular housing 101 that developed to be positioned over a food that is to be decorated. The housing 101 as mentioned herein is an enclosure encasing various components associated with the device, wherein the housing 101 is made up of material that includes but not limited to stainless steel, which in turn ensures that the device is of generous size and is light in weight.

[0024] The housing 101 features multiple compartments 102, that are accessed by the user to store multiple decorative edible ingredients, such as white chocolate, dark chocolate, colorful icing and alike, for use in decorating the food. 

[0025] The housing 101 is installed with an inbuilt microcontroller that is wirelessly linked with a computing unit associated with the device via a communication module. The communication module mentioned herein includes, but not limited to Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) module, Bluetooth module, GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) module for enabling the user to input commands regarding various decorations that are to be made over the food.

[0026] In order to activate functioning of the device, a user is required to manually switch on the device by pressing a button positioned on the housing 101, wherein the button used herein is a push button. Upon pressing of the button, the circuits get closed allowing conduction of electricity that leads to activation of the device and vice versa.

[0001] Upon activation of the device by the user, a user-interface installed within the computing unit is accessed by the user to input commands regarding various decorations that are to be made over the food.  The user-interactive provides a series of questions regarding various decorations that are to be made over the food. The user either selects from a list of options provided on the display or manually enters the details, wherein the user is required to enter details such as a various decorations that are to be made over the food. Based on input commands of the user, the microcontroller determines a pattern along which the ingredients are to be poured over the food item.

[0002] An artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 103 mounted on the body is activated by the microcontroller to detect dimensions and exact positioning of the food item. The imaging unit 103 comprises of an image capturing arrangement including a set of lenses that captures multiple images in surrounding of the housing 101, and the captured images are stored within memory of the imaging unit 103 in form of an optical data. 

[0003] The imaging unit 103 also comprises of a processor that is integrated with artificial intelligence protocols, such that the processor processes the optical data and extracts the required data from the captured images. The extracted data is further converted into digital pulses and bits and are further transmitted to the microcontroller. The microcontroller processes the received data and determines dimensions and exact positioning of the food item in proximity. 

[0004] Based on the determined dimensions and positioning of the food item, the microcontroller activates a holographic projection unit 104 mounted over the body to project a holographic image in view of guiding the user to move the body along the evaluated pattern over the food item.

[0005] A proximity sensor installed on the body detects positioning of the body over the food item. The proximity sensor used herein is preferably an ultrasonic proximity sensor that uses ultrasonic waves to detect the positioning of the body over the food item. The ultrasonic proximity sensor typically emits ultrasonic waves towards the surrounding, the ultrasonic waves hit the food item and bounce back to the sensor’s receiver. 

[0006] The receiver of the ultrasonic proximity sensor is sensitive to the emitted ultrasonic waves and listens for the reflected waves. When the emitted ultrasonic waves are received by the receiver the proximity sensor sends the data to the microcontroller which processes and analyzes the acquired data to detect positioning of the body over the food item.

[0007] In accordance to the detected positioning of the body over the food item, a motorized iris unit 105 crafted on each of the compartments 102, along circumference of the housing 101 are actuated by the microcontroller to get opened for allowing decorative edibles to get dispensed over the food item. The motorized iris unit 105 typically refers to the iris or aperture mechanism in the camera or optical instruments as it works in a similar manner to that of a human eye. The iris unit 105 consists several thin and overlapping blades that forms an adjustable opening of the lid. Upon actuation of the motorized iris unit 105 by the microcontroller the blades move apart resulting in the widening of mouth portion, allowing the decorative ingredients to get dispensed over the food item.

[0008] A hollow extendable pole 106 installed in continuation to the iris unit 105 is actuated by the microcontroller to get extended in view of positioning mouth portion of the pole 106 in proximity to the food item for appropriate dispensing the ingredients over the food item. The extension of the pole 106 is operated by the microcontroller by employing a drawer arrangement installed within the pole 106. 

[0009] The drawer arrangement consists of multiple plates that are overlapped to each other with a sliding unit, wherein upon actuation of the drawer arrangement by the microcontroller, the motor in the sliding unit starts rotating a wheel coupled via a shaft in clockwise/anticlockwise direction providing a movement to the slider in the drawer arrangement to extend pole 106 in view of positioning mouth portion of the pole 106 in proximity to the food item for appropriate dispensing the ingredients over the food item.

[0010] The body is installed with a pressure sensor that detects pressure applied by the user for squeezing the ingredients out of the compartment. The pressure sensor comprises of a sensing element known as diaphragm that experiences a force exerted by the user for squeezing the ingredients out of the compartment. This force leads to deflection in the diaphragm that is measured by the sensor and converted into an electrical signal which is sent to the microcontroller for detecting pressure applied by the user for squeezing the ingredients out of the compartment. 

[0011] In case the detected is pressure is monitored to recede a threshold amount, as stored within a database linked with the microcontroller, the microcontroller regulates energization/de-energization of plurality of electromagnetic springs 107 configured inside the body for applying an optimum pressure for pouring the ingredient out of the compartment. 

[0012] The electromagnetic springs 107 is a specialized type of spring in which the magnetic field is produced by an electric current. When the current is passed through the spring, it creates a magnetic field around the spring, thus energizing/de-energizing the springs 107 for applying an optimum pressure for pouring the ingredient out of the compartment.

[0013] A speaker 108 mounted on the body is activated by the microcontroller to produce audio notification for guiding the user to move body over the food item along the specified pattern. The speaker 108 works by receiving signals from the microcontroller, converting them into sound waves through a diaphragm’s vibration, and producing audible sounds with the help of amplification and control circuitry in order to notify the user to move body over the food item along the specified pattern.

[0014] Each of the compartments 102 is embedded with a level sensor that detects level of ingredients stored inside the compartments 102. The level sensor used herein is a pressure-based level sensor which works on the principle that the pressure exerted by a liquid at a specific depth is directly proportional to the height of the liquid column in the sensor. The pressure-based level sensor comprises of a piezoelectric sensing element. 

[0015] When the sensing element is exposed to the liquid within the sensor, some hydrostatic pressure is exerted on the element by the liquid and which varies in accordance to the height of the liquid. A pressure transducer converts the hydrostatic pressure exerted by the liquid into an electrical pulse. Further the microcontroller analyses the electrical signal and based on which determine the level of the ingredients remaining in the compartments 102 and in case the detected level recedes a threshold value, the microcontroller sends an alert notification on the computing unit for notifying the user to refill the compartments 102.

[0016]  Lastly, a battery is installed within the device which is connected to the microcontroller that supplies current to all the electrically powered components that needs an amount of electric power to perform their functions and operation in an efficient manner. The battery utilized here, is preferably a dry battery which is made up of Lithium-ion material that gives the device a long-lasting as well as an efficient DC (Direct Current) current which helps every component to function properly in an efficient manner. As the device is battery operated and do not need any electrical voltage for functioning. Hence the presence of battery leads to the portability of the device i.e., user is able to place as well as moves the device from one place to another as per the requirements.
