BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION:
Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a metabolic disorder resulting from a defect in insulin secretion, insulin action, or both. Insulin deficiency in turn leads to chronic hyperglycaemia with disturbances of carbohydrate, fat, and protein metabolism. Diabetes is the most common endocrine disorder, that is, multifaceted condition that includes ß-cell dysfunction, neurotransmitter dysfunction, decreased insulin secretion, decreased incretin effect, increased hepatic glucose production, increased glucagon secretion, decreased glucose uptake, peripheral insulin resistance, and elevated hepatic gluconeogenesis together with hypertension, dyslipidemia, obesity, and cardiovascular disease. As the disease progresses, tissue or vascular damage ensues leading to severe diabetic complications such as retinopathy, neuropathy, and nephropathy. The prevalence of diabetes is rising all over the world due to population growth, aging, urbanisation, and an increase of obesity and physical inactivity. The International Diabetes Federation (IDF) estimates the total number of people in India with diabetes to be around 50.8 million in 2010 rising to 87.0 million by 2030. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) presents a major challenge to healthcare system around the world. The current oral treatment options for T2DM include metformin, sulfonylurea or thiazolidinedione derivatives, glycosidase inhibitors, and the recently dipeptidyl peptidase IV inhibitors which have been introduced. Antioxidants are used as supportive therapy in the treatment of DM and hypoglycemic plants have been shown to regulate the oxidative complications of DM (Datar et al., Design and synthesis of pyrazole-3-one derivatives as hypoglycaemic agents. Int J Med Chem 2015:1–10). The a-glucosidase is a validated target to develop drugs for treating type 2 diabetes mellitus. The existing a-glucosidase inhibitors have certain shortcomings related to side effects and route of synthesis. Accordingly, it is inevitable to develop new chemical templates as a-glucosidase inhibitors. 

Pyrazole derivatives have a special place in medicinal chemistry because of various biological activities. Recently, pyrazole-based heterocyclic compounds have emerged as a promising scaffold to develop a-glucosidase inhibitors. The pyrazole ring is a prominent structural motif found in numerous pharmaceutically active compounds. This is mainly due to its ease of preparation and pharmacological activity. It has also been found that the selective functionalization of pyrazole with diverse substituents improves their range of action in various fields. As a part of the continuing interest in pyrazole derivatives, numerous compounds with pyrazole rings have been reported.  Some of the prior art disclosing the pyrazole and thiazole derivatives have been listed below.

US7256209B2 discloses the synthesis of new pyrazole-O-glycoside derivatives and pyrazole-O-glucuronide derivatives wherein glucose (namely, ß-D-glucopyranose) or glucuronic acid (namely, ß-D-glucopyranoside uronic acid) is bonded to pyrazole, and vigorously investigates the action of those derivatives on urinary sugar excretion. As the result of animal tests, it was found that the synthesized derivatives compounds act on urinary sugar excretion. 

WO2009034388A1 discloses heterocyclic compounds which have dual activity as agonists of GPRl 19 and inhibitors of DPP-IV and are useful for the treatment of metabolic disorders including type II diabetes.

US4687777A discloses thiazolidinedione derivatives of the formula: ##STR1## and pharmacologically acceptable salts thereof are novel compounds, which exhibit in mammals blood sugar and lipid lowering activity, and are of value as a therapeutic agent for treatment of diabetes and hyperlipemia.

Most of the pyrazole derivatives disclosed in prior art show antidiabetic activity. However, these molecules primarily exhibit some shortcomings such as moderate efficacy, off-target effects, poor solubility, and metabolic instability. Many of the disclosed molecules suffer from poor water solubility, leading to formulation challenges and reduced bioavailability, which limited their effectiveness in clinical settings. The derivatives showed limited activity against multiple biological targets, primarily focusing on inhibiting a single pathway (such as PPAR receptors). This narrow mechanism of action limited their overall effectiveness in complex metabolic disorders like diabetes. Moreover, the molecules display moderate efficacy and a high potential for drug resistance over prolonged use. Additionally, the metabolic instability of the derivatives led to rapid clearance from the body, necessitating frequent dosing. Unlike prior art focusing solely on glycemic control. Thus, there is a need to design and develop pyrazole derivatives that can overcome the drawbacks of molecules disclosed in prior art.

A series of novel 1H-pyrazole derivatives linked to 4-methylthiazole-5-carboxylate (VA-P) were designed and synthesized as potential a-glucosidase inhibitors. Their inhibitory activity was evaluated through both in-silico and in-vitro studies. Inhibition assays revealed IC50 values ranging from 88.2 µM to 102.6 µM for all molecules, compared to the standard inhibitor acarbose (IC50 = 75.8 µM). At the highest tested concentration, molecules VK, VM, and VN exhibited the greatest inhibition percentages of 87.4%, 85.3%, and 90.5%, respectively. These molecules also achieved higher induced-fit docking (IFD) scores than acarbose, with VN, VM, and VK scoring -1529.63, -1526.37, and -1525.70 Kcal/mol, respectively. VN emerged as the most potent molecule, showing favorable in vivo bioactivity with an IC50 of 93.66 µM, closely comparable to acarbose. Molecular dynamics and MM-GBSA analysis of VN revealed key interactions, including hydrogen bonding with Trp299 and Glu330, hydrophobic interactions with Trp169 and Phe481, and a water bridge involving Glu377, which contributed to its potent a-glucosidase inhibition. Overall, these synthesized derivatives show great promise as potential candidates for further development as novel a-glucosidase inhibitors.

The novel 1H-pyrazole derivatives linked to 4-methylthiazole-5-carboxylate (VA-P) compounds VK, VM, and VN have been synthesized and tested in vivo using Streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic wistar rats. The results of in vivo study showed that compounds VK and VN demonstrated significant (p < 0.0001) reductions in blood glucose levels, improvement in plasma insulin, and reduction in HbA1c%, compared to the untreated diabetic group. Furthermore, VN exhibited superior efficacy compared to VK and acarbose in regulating glucose metabolism, lipid profiles (LDL/HDL, total cholesterol, and triglycerides), and reducing liver enzymes (SGOT, SGPT, ALP) to near-normal levels. Histopathological analysis showed a marked improvement in pancreatic ß-cell regeneration, and a reduction in liver and kidney inflammation in VN-treated animals.

Induction of Type 2 diabetes
Diabetes was induced in groups II through VI via a solitary intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of streptozotocin (STZ) at a 60 mg/kg concentration, dissolved in a 0.1 M sodium citrate buffer at pH 4.5. Determination of animal weight and biochemical parameters
The body weight and an array of biochemical parameters, encompassing blood glucose, insulin, creatinine, HbA1c, and lipid profile, were assessed for each experimental subject on Day 3 and Day 28. The parameters were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kits, adhering to the manufacturer's prescribed protocol.

Histopathological analysis
Upon the conclusion of the experimental period, specifically after 28 days, the animals were anesthetized and subsequently euthanized. In vivo antidiabetic activity
In the present invention, the anti-diabetic potential of synthesized compounds was evaluated using male Albino Wistar rats (200-240 g) as subjects. The experimental animals were divided into six groups (I-VI), each consisting of six rats (n=6), as outlined below: Group I: Healthy control; Group II: Positive control (STZ); Group III: Diabetes-induced group treated with the standard drug acarbose (10 mg/kg body weight); Group IV: Diabetes-induced group treated with compound VK; Group V: Diabetes-induced group treated with compound VM; Group VI: Diabetes-induced group treated with compound VN. Each group was housed in individual cages under controlled conditions of 24 ± 3 °C, 65 ± 5% relative humidity, and a 12-hour day-night cycle. Various parameters, including body weight, blood glucose levels, plasma insulin, HbA1c%, serum creatinine, and the LDL/HDL ratio, were assessed for each group on Day 3 and Day 28.

Effect of synthesized compounds on body weight
Metabolic changes caused by diabetes may affect weight regulation, making it essential to monitor the weight of experimental animals when assessing the impact of drugs being tested. After a 28-day experimental period, a significant reduction in body weight (p < 0.0001) was observed in the diabetic group compared to the healthy control group. Treatment with compound VN resulted in a significant improvement (p < 0.0001) in body weight compared to the diabetic group. Additionally, a notable increase (p < 0.01) in body weight was observed in the VK-treated group compared to the diabetic group. In contrast, no significant changes were detected in the VM-treated group when compared to the diabetic group (figure 3A). These results indicate that compounds VK and VN positively affect body weight regulation in diabetic rats, possibly due to insulin secretion and glucose uptake improvements.

Effect of synthesized compounds on blood glucose level
After three days of STZ administration, a significant increase in blood glucose levels (p < 0.0001) was observed in the positive control group compared to the healthy control group. Following 28 days of treatment, diabetic rats treated with compound VK showed a significant reduction (p < 0.001) in blood glucose levels compared to the diabetic group. The most considerable decrease (p < 0.0001) in blood glucose levels was observed in rats treated with compound VN compared to the diabetic group. Moreover, the results of the VN-treated group after the 28-day treatment period were similar to those of the acarbose-treated group. In contrast, no significant effect on blood glucose levels was found with compound VM (figure 3B). These findings suggest compound VN exhibits superior blood glucose control compared to the other two synthesized molecules.

Effect of synthesized compounds on plasma insulin level 
A significant decrease in plasma insulin levels was noticed three days after STZ administration compared to the healthy group. After a 28-day treatment period, diabetic rats treated with compound VN showed a significant increase (p < 0.05) in plasma insulin levels compared to the diabetic group, as illustrated in figure 3C. Both VK and VM-treated groups demonstrated a moderate increase in serum insulin levels after 28 days of treatment; however, the increase was not statistically significant compared to the diabetic control group. The rise in plasma insulin levels suggests that the synthesized compounds enhance insulin production and sensitivity, leading to increased glucose uptake by tissues and, consequently, lower plasma glucose levels. 

Effect of synthesized compounds on HbA1c level 
A significant increase (p < 0.0001) in HbA1c was observed in the diabetic group compared to the healthy control group. After the 28-day experimental period, a significant decrease in HbA1c levels was seen in both the VK-treated group (p < 0.01) and the VN-treated group (p < 0.0001) when compared to the diabetic group (figure 3D). This result highlights the anti-diabetic potential of compounds VK and VN, with VN proving to be the most effective compound.

Effect of synthesized compounds on lipid profile
Diabetes is linked to changes in lipid metabolism due to insulin resistance. Insulin resistance encourages the production of triglyceride-rich VLDL in the liver, which may lead to the creation of LDL (low-density lipoprotein, or "bad cholesterol"). Additionally, insulin resistance affects the activity of lipoprotein lipase, an enzyme responsible for breaking down triglycerides, accumulating LDL, and decreasing HDL (high-density lipoprotein) levels. These observations were evident in the current study, where a significant (p < 0.01) increase in the LDL/HDL ratio was observed in the diabetic group compared to the healthy control group. Treatment with synthesized compounds led to a moderate decrease in the LDL/HDL ratio after 28 days of treatment (figure 6E), indicating their positive impact on lipid metabolism. The impact of synthesized compounds, namely VK, VM, and VN, on total cholesterol and triglyceride concentrations, following a 28-day treatment period is demonstrated in figure 6F. A substantial elevation in total cholesterol and triglyceride levels was observed in the streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic cohort when compared to the healthy control group, with the difference reaching statistical significance (p<0.0001). Notably, a marked reduction in total cholesterol and triglyceride concentrations was observed after 28 days of treatment with VK (p<0.01) and VN (p<0.0001), thus indicating their favorable influence on the lipid profiles of the treated animals in comparison to the diabetic cohort. Conversely, no significant variation in total cholesterol and triglyceride levels was detected following treatment with compound VM.

A noteworthy elevation (p<0.0001) in the activities of serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (SGOT), serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase (SGPT), and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) was observed in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic rats in comparison to the healthy control group. Following a 28-day treatment period with the synthesized compounds, a decrease in the levels of SGOT, SGPT, and ALP was detected about the diabetic cohort. However, a significant reduction was observed in the VK (0.001) and VN (0.0001) groups (Figure 6G). Bilirubin is produced as a result of hemoglobin catabolism. The heightened levels of total and direct bilirubin in diabetic rats compared to the normal control group are indicative of liver disease. The considerable (p<0.05) decrease in total and direct bilirubin levels to normal concentrations after 28 days of VK and VN treatment demonstrates the advantageous effects of these compounds on liver function. Nevertheless, no significant variation in bilirubin levels was detected following VM administration in diabetic rats in comparison to the disease group (figure 6H).
Effect of synthesized compounds on kidney function (serum creatinine and serum urea level)
Serum creatinine and urea concentrations are crucial for assessing the glomerular filtration rate. A significant (p < 0.0001) increase in serum creatinine and urea levels was observed in the diabetic cohort compared to the healthy control group, suggesting metabolic disruption and renal dysfunction in the diabetic population. This can be attributed to the detrimental effects of elevated plasma glucose concentrations on renal function, which impairs creatinine and urea excretion. Following a 28-day treatment period with compound VN, a substantial (p < 0.01) decrease in plasma creatinine levels was detected in comparison to the diabetic group, yielding results like to those in the acarbose-treated group (Figure 7I). This finding highlights the potential benefits of VN in addressing diabetic complications. Nevertheless, no significant impact on creatinine levels was observed after administering compounds VK and VM. Moreover, a significant reduction in serum urea levels was detected after 28 days of treatment in diabetic rats treated with VK (p<0.01) and VN (p<0.0001) compared to the diabetic control group, demonstrating their capacity to mitigate the detrimental effects of diabetes on renal function (figure 7J).

Abstract:

A system for enhanced big data analytics is disclosed. The system includes a distributed processing engine configured to ingest and transform heterogeneous data streams from a plurality of sources, including structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data. Further, the system includes a machine learning orchestrator operatively coupled to the distributed processing engine, the orchestrator configured to automate training, validation, and deployment of machine learning models across distributed compute nodes. The system includes an adaptive resource allocation module employing reinforcement learning to dynamically scale compute, memory, and storage resources based on real-time workload demands and predictive analytics. A hybrid storage engine integrating columnar databases, graph-based caches, and object storage, wherein the storage engine partitions data into hot and cold tiers based on access frequency and optimizes I/O operations via adaptive compression. A security layer implementing encrypted data sharding and role-based access control to secure data during ingestion, processing, and storage.

Description:TECHNICAL FIELD
[001] The present invention relates generally to field of big data analytics, specifically systems and methods for enhanced big data analytics.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[002] Traditional big data analytics systems rely heavily on batch-oriented processing frameworks optimized for static, homogeneous datasets. These systems struggle with dynamic, real-time workloads generated by modern applications like IoT sensors, social media feeds, or financial transactions. For instance, while Spark Streaming enables micro-batching, it introduces latency due to fixed time windows and lacks native integration with machine learning (ML) pipelines, requiring manual model deployment and retraining. Similarly, streaming platforms but do not inherently support adaptive resource scaling or automated ML workflows, leading to inefficiencies in handling fluctuating workloads.
[003] Resource allocation in legacy systems often employs static partitioning of computational resources, which fails to account for variable data volumes or heterogeneous workloads. This results in underutilized clusters during low-demand periods and bottlenecks during peak loads. Hybrid storage solutions, attempt to unify structured and unstructured data but lack intelligent tiering mechanisms to optimize for access patterns (e.g., hot vs. cold data), causing unnecessary I/O overhead. Furthermore, existing systems inadequately address data quality challenges, particularly with unstructured text, images, or log files. Tools like perform basic extraction and cleansing but lack context-aware tagging, such as using NLP to auto-classify sentiment in social media data or identify anomalies in log streams.
[004] Machine learning integration in prior systems is often siloed, requiring separate platforms  to train models offline, followed by manual deployment into production pipelines. This disconnection delays model updates and hinders real-time analytics. Security remains another critical gap: while encryption tools like Apache Knox or Kerberos secure data at rest, distributed processing across edge devices or multi-cloud environments exposes vulnerabilities during data sharding or in-memory computation. Federated learning frameworks, enable decentralized model training but lack tight coupling with resource allocators to balance edge-device constraints (e.g., power, bandwidth) with global model accuracy.
[005] Finally, visualization tools focus on post-processing dashboards but lack native support for interactive, real-time rendering of analytics results, particularly in immersive formats. Data lineage tracking, even with tools often omits granular audit trails for transformations applied in distributed environments, complicating compliance with regulations. Collectively, these limitations in scalability, latency, automation, and security underscore the need for a unified system that integrates adaptive resource management, ML-driven analytics, and secure, real-time processing across heterogeneous data sources.
[006] Therefore, there is need to develop a system and method that overcome the aforementioned technical problems.

The device comprises a rigid frame, an electric motor, a camshaft with a spiral or eccentric profile, a follower arm, and a vertically mounted hammer. As the motor rotates the camshaft, the follower arm transmits reciprocating motion to the hammer, causing it to cyclically strike downward onto a bark sample placed on an anvil beneath it. Description:TECHNICAL FIELD
[001] The present invention relates generally to field wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and 5G telecommunications, specifically systems and methods for environment monitoring.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[002] Existing environmental monitoring systems often rely on traditional wireless technologies. The existing environmental monitoring systems face limitations in scalability, latency, coverage, and energy efficiency, particularly in large-scale or densely populated deployments. For example, the existing environmental monitoring systems suffer from low data rates, making them unsuitable for real-time monitoring of high-frequency environmental changes.
[003] The existing environmental monitoring systems consume excessive power for continuous data streaming and struggle with network congestion in dense sensor deployments. Legacy WSNs lack interoperability with modern IoT ecosystems and often require complex gateway infrastructure for data aggregation. The existing environmental monitoring systems fail to address the integration of edge computing with 5G’s ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) and massive machine-type communication (mMTC) capabilities. 
[004] Additionally, conventional power management strategies do not adaptively optimize energy use based on dynamic 5G network conditions (e.g., switching between millimeter-wave and sub-6 GHz bands).
[005] Therefore, there is need to develop a system and method that overcome the aforementioned technical problems.

This invention relates to an ai-based automated drug dosage calculation and risk assessment system for pharmacists and healthcare providers.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
The AI-Driven Drug Dosage & Risk Assessment System introduces an advanced, intelligent solution for personalized medication management, integrating AI-driven analytics, biometric authentication, and real-time patient monitoring. This innovation leverages machine learning algorithms and natural language processing to analyze patient health parameters, medical history, and prescription data, ensuring precise drug dosage recommendations while minimizing adverse drug interactions and risk factors. The system incorporates secure data processing, real-time physiological monitoring, and interactive user interfaces, enabling healthcare providers to make informed decisions with enhanced accuracy and efficiency. Designed for seamless integration into pharmacies, hospitals, and telemedicine platforms, this solution enhances patient safety, optimizes medication adherence, and supports data-driven clinical decision-making in modern healthcare environments.
The AI-Driven Drug Dosage & Risk Assessment System addresses critical challenges in modern healthcare, including medication errors, adverse drug interactions, and the lack of personalized dosage recommendations. Traditional prescription methods often rely on generalized guidelines, which may not account for individual patient factors such as age, weight, organ function, allergies, or existing health conditions. Additionally, pharmacists and healthcare providers face difficulties in assessing drug compatibility and potential side effects in real-time, increasing the risk of medication-related complications. This innovation provides an AI-powered solution that automates dosage calculations, analyzes patient-specific data, and detects potential risks before medication administration. By integrating real-time monitoring and intelligent decision-making, the system enhances patient safety, reduces hospital readmissions due to medication errors, and improves overall healthcare efficiency.

This invention relates to an ai-based pharmacovigilance and adverse drug reaction monitoring system for patient safety.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
This advance system is a smart edge-based healthcare innovation designed to detect, monitor, and report adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in real-time using embedded artificial intelligence and machine learning. This system continuously collects patient health data, observes behavior and physiological cues, and applies pre-trained AI models to identify potential ADRs early. It operates autonomously at the edge while maintaining a secure connection to a custom cloud server that allows for dynamic model training using the latest population-level data. This innovation enhances pharmacovigilance by enabling continuous, real-time monitoring and intelligent risk assessment, significantly improving patient safety in both clinical and remote environments.
The system addresses the growing concern of undetected and underreported adverse drug reactions (ADRs), which contribute significantly to patient harm, increased hospitalization, and healthcare costs. Traditional pharmacovigilance systems are largely reactive, dependent on manual reporting by healthcare professionals or patients, often leading to delayed identification of drug-related risks. Moreover, these systems lack continuous monitoring and real-time analysis, making it difficult to detect subtle or early symptoms of ADRs. This invention fills that gap by providing an AI-powered, real-time monitoring solution that operates independently at the edge, continuously analyzing patient responses and environmental context to detect potential ADRs as they occur. By enabling proactive intervention and timely reporting, the system enhances patient safety, supports clinicians in making informed decisions, and strengthens the overall pharmacovigilance infrastructure.

This system operates through a single advanced edge node, named the AI-Driven Pharmacovigilance & ADR Monitoring Node (ADRMON Node), which continuously observes patient behavior and physiological changes post-medication to identify potential ADRs early and accurately. The ADRMON Node integrates a variety of components including the Raspberry Pi Board, 128GB MicroSD Card Module, Touch TFT Display, Raspberry Pi SSD Kit, Raspberry Pi AI Hat, Camera Module, GSM Dual Communication Module, 4-Channel ReSpeaker Module, Speaker Module, and Power Supply. The Camera Module serves as an observation tool that captures facial expressions and physical cues, such as allergic reactions, rashes, or discomfort, which are critical in detecting visible signs of ADRs. Simultaneously, the ReSpeaker Module, with its four-channel microphone array, is used to capture voice feedback from patients, enabling the system to understand complaints, discomfort, or symptoms expressed verbally. These voice inputs are processed in real-time using AI algorithms running on the Raspberry Pi AI Hat, which enables faster inference and enhances the accuracy of ADR detection. The Touch TFT Display provides an intuitive interface where the system logs alerts, asks follow-up questions, and displays summaries of potential adverse reactions.
The GSM Dual Communication Module plays a critical role in maintaining real-time connectivity with the central custom cloud server, allowing for periodic synchronization of data and continuous improvement of the AI model. The Power Supply ensures uninterrupted operation, making the device suitable for hospital use, in-home monitoring, or remote healthcare environments.In operation, once a patient receives medication, the ADRMON Node begins passive monitoring using the Camera Module and ReSpeaker Module. Any unusual activity—such as a change in skin condition, facial distress, verbal complaints like “I feel dizzy” or “my heart is racing”—is captured and processed using the AI engine. If an adverse reaction is suspected, the system notifies the patient and care provider via the Speaker Module, logs the incident on the TFT Display, and simultaneously transmits the data to the cloud server using the GSM Module. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
This solution involves a smart ingestible capsule designed to monitor real-time drug absorption within a patient’s body. The capsule is equipped with a set of advanced sensors to detect critical parameters such as pH levels, temperature, and conductivity, providing detailed insights into the gastrointestinal environment and drug absorption process. The device communicates wirelessly with external systems, enabling continuous monitoring and data transmission for healthcare providers. A compact, rechargeable power source ensures prolonged operation, while an integrated identification system enables secure tracking and monitoring of the capsule throughout the digestive process. This technology aims to improve personalized medicine by offering precise and real-time feedback on drug absorption, optimizing treatment outcomes.
The proposed solution addresses the challenge of monitoring drug absorption in real-time, a critical factor in the effectiveness of oral medications. Currently, there is no reliable, non-invasive method to track how drugs are absorbed in the body, leading to inefficiencies in treatment plans, dosing errors, and a lack of personalized medication management. Patients with varying metabolic rates, gastrointestinal conditions, or those on complex medication regimens may experience different absorption rates, which can affect the efficacy and safety of the treatment. By providing real-time data on drug absorption, this technology enables healthcare providers to optimize dosing, reduce adverse reactions, and tailor treatments to individual patient needs, ultimately improving overall therapeutic outcomes.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
This innovation provides a comprehensive, AI-powered, and blockchain-based digital microfinance lending and credit assessment platform designed to enhance financial inclusion. The system includes two integrated nodes that work seamlessly to facilitate secure, efficient, and transparent microfinance lending. The first node leverages advanced AI and blockchain technology to manage the lending process, utilizing real-time data and machine learning for automated loan approvals, risk assessment, and smart contract execution. The second node offers a dynamic visualization and analytics interface that enables users to view detailed credit assessments, financial health reports, and lending performance metrics. By connecting both nodes to a cloud-based server, the system enables continuous learning and improvement, ensuring accurate credit assessments, transparent lending decisions, and streamlined microfinance operations.
This innovation addresses the challenge of providing accessible, secure, and transparent financial services to underserved communities, particularly in the microfinance sector. Traditional lending systems often lack efficiency, transparency, and scalability, leaving many individuals and small businesses without access to necessary capital. By combining blockchain technology with AI-driven credit assessment, this innovation streamlines the lending process, automates decision-making, and ensures accurate and fair lending practices. It solves the problem of limited access to credit for individuals in emerging markets and promotes financial inclusion, allowing microfinance institutions to offer personalized, data-backed loan products at scale.
